title: Tight security exponent for bounded-storage privacy amplification
summary: Determine the exact total-variation security exponent of randomized privacy amplification when an eavesdropper stores a rate-limited encoding of correlated side information.

formal_statement.body: Let $(X^n,Y^n)\sim P_{XY}^{\otimes n}$ over finite alphabets. A rate-$R_1$ randomized universal hash $F_n$ produces $K_n=F_n(X^n)\in\{0,1\}^{nR_1}$, while Eve stores $S_n=g_n(Y^n)\in\{0,1\}^{nR_2}$. With $\Delta_n=d_{\mathrm{var}}(P_{K_nS_nF_n},P_{\mathrm{unif}}\times P_{S_n}\times P_{F_n})$, determine the exact optimal worst-case exponent $E_{\mathrm{sec}}(R_1,R_2\mid P_{XY})$ of $\Delta_n$ under the source's admissible hashing model and all rate-$R_2$ storage maps $g_n$. Prove matching achievable and converse exponent bounds throughout the source-defined secure rate region; in particular, decide when the exponent implicit in Theorem 3 is tight.

scope.domain: Information-theoretic privacy amplification against a bounded-storage eavesdropper with correlated side information
assumptions: X^n and Y^n are finite-alphabet i.i.d. correlated sources with law P_XY
The distilled key has rate R1 and uses the source's randomized universal-hashing model
Eve stores an arbitrary rate-R2 encoding g_n(Y^n)
Security is measured by the total-variation criterion in equation (106)
scope.unresolved_remainder: A matching converse for the total-variation security exponent is not known over the full source-defined secure rate region. Theorem 3 supplies an exponential upper bound on the security criterion, but its exact optimal worst-case exponent and the conditions for tightness remain open.

citations.label: Takeuchi--Watanabe, Tight Exponential Strong Converse for Source Coding Problem With Encoded Side Information
citations.locator: Section VI and conclusion, journal pp. 1542-1544, Theorem 3 and equation (119)

progress.summary: The source derives an exponential total-variation security bound for the bounded-storage model and explicitly leaves derivation of the tight exponential security bound as a future agenda.
